knowledge:
- key_parameters: listEX=A list of expression matrices, dataframes, or ExpressionSets ;; listPheno=A list of phenodata dataframes (can be NULL if listEX contains ExpressionSets) ;; namePheno=Column names or positions in pheno identifying the comparison groups ;; expGroups=Experimental group names or positions ;; refGroups=Reference group names or positions ;; finalID=Target gene ID format ("GeneSymbol", "Entrez", "Ensembl") ;; organism=Organism name for gene ID mapping ;; typeMethod=Meta-analysis method ("FEM", "REM", "Fisher", "Stouffer", "maxP", "minP", "ACAT") ;; missAllow=Maximum proportion of missing values allowed per sample ;; proportionData=Minimum proportion of datasets a gene must be present in ;; scaling=Scaling method for heatmap ("zscor", "swr", "rscale", "none")
- alternatives: swamp package (prince and prince.plot) is used for visualizing batch effects before correction ;; limma package is recommended for RNA-Seq normalization prior to DExMA analysis
- when_to_use: Use when combining multiple independent transcriptomic datasets (microarray or normalized RNA-Seq) to identify robust differentially expressed genes, especially when datasets have different gene annotations or missing genes.
- pitfalls: Ensure all datasets are log2-transformed (using dataLog) and mapped to the same gene ID (using allSameID) before running meta-analysis. Always perform a heterogeneity test (heterogeneityTest) to choose between Fixed Effects Model (FEM) and Random Effects Model (REM). Samples not belonging to either experimental or reference groups are excluded during object creation.

workflows.name: standard_meta_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform a complete gene expression meta-analysis workflow including data preparation, annotation harmonization, log transformation, heterogeneity testing, optional imputation, meta-analysis, and heatmap visualization.
workflows.stages: 1. Create meta-analysis object ;; 2. Harmonize gene IDs ;; 3. Log-transform data ;; 4. Test for heterogeneity ;; 5. Impute missing genes (optional) ;; 6. Perform meta-analysis ;; 7. Visualize results via heatmap
workflows.code:
phenoGroups = c("condition", "condition", "state", "state")
phenoCases = list(Study1 = "Diseased", Study2 = c("Diseased", "ill"),
                    Study3 = "Diseased", Study4 = "ill")
phenoControls = list(Study1 = "Healthy", Study2 = c("Healthy", "control"),
                    Study3 = "Healthy", Study4 = "control")
newObjectMA <- createObjectMA(listEX=listMatrixEX,
                                listPheno = listPhenodatas,
                                namePheno=phenoGroups,
                                expGroups=phenoCases, 
                                refGroups = phenoControls)
newObjectMA <- allSameID(newObjectMA, finalID="GeneSymbol", organism = "Homo sapiens")
newObjectMA <- dataLog(newObjectMA)
heterogeneityTest(newObjectMA)
imputation <- missGenesImput(maObject, k =7)
maObject_imput <- imputation$objectMA
resultsMA <- metaAnalysisDE(newObjectMA, typeMethod="REM",
                            missAllow=0.3, proportionData=0.50)
makeHeatmap(objectMA=newObjectMA, resMA=resultsMA, scaling = "zscor", 
            regulation = "all", numSig=40,
            fdrSig = 0.05, logFCSig = 1.5, show_rownames = TRUE)

workflows.name: batch_effect_correction
workflows.intent: Detect and remove batch effects from individual datasets and calculate individual study effect sizes or p-values.
workflows.stages: 1. Detect batch effects using principal components ;; 2. Remove batch effects ;; 3. Calculate individual study effect sizes ;; 4. Calculate individual study p-values
workflows.code:
library(swamp)
pheno <- listPhenodatas$Study2
pheno <- pheno[,apply(pheno,2,function(x) length(table(x)))>1]
pheno <- data.frame(apply(pheno, 2, factor), stringsAsFactors = TRUE) 
res_prince <- prince(listMatrixEX$Study2, pheno,top=ncol(listMatrixEX$Study2))
prince.plot(res_prince,note=TRUE , notecex=0.5)
listMatrixEX$Study2 <- batchRemove(listMatrixEX$Study2, listPhenodatas$Study2, 
                                    formula=~gender+race, 
                                    mainCov = "race", nameGroup="condition")
effects <- calculateES(newObjectMA)
pvalues <- pvalueIndAnalysis(newObjectMA)
